question: Do document-side savings persist across fresh target processes when input validation and state reading are timed explicitly?
claim: Matched document-side reconstruction time, not physical index rebuild time.
gap: Current independent measurements are one pass and omit state-hash validation from replay time.
setup: Same frozen full-collection pages and source state bytes; same target, processor, A100, BF16, batch 1. Three fresh target processes; alternate raw/replay order by page and round.
scope: All 2840 frozen pages per round; 8520 paired page checks. Approximately 6–12 A100 hours including repeated model loading and validation, subject to shared host load. No new dataset or model family.
timing_includes: page image-byte validation and image preprocessing for raw
saved-state hash verification and warm state read for replay
host/device transfer and synchronized target computation
timing_excludes: model loading and static artifact verification
output serialization and physical index construction
cache: Natural warm state-read path; do not flush system caches or relabel as cold IO.
reporting: Per-round totals and all three ratios; median and range across rounds. Pages are not repeated-run uncertainty samples. Log co-resident GPU processes.
failure_interpretation: Preserve all unequal pages and all timing rounds. If variance or active competing load dominates, do not publish a single headline ratio; timing does not rescue a fidelity failure.
